title: A merged memory
description: One memory in the merged output (`memories.jsonl` of a run). It carries the merge-only corroboration counts under `provenance.corroboration`, so it validates merged output; the per-arm files under `arms/` hold the same content fields flat (`scope_level`, `temporal_kind`, ...) and are not validated against it. A memory is one durable thing worth remembering, learned in a conversation and backed by verified quotes. Every field is either MODEL-EMITTED (the model proposes it; code validates or softens it) or CODE-STAMPED (code owns it: identity, provenance, corroboration, the evidence gate). TAGS: `tags` is a typed object over six axes. This is memory format v3.

memory_id.description: CODE-STAMPED stable identity: the first 24 hex chars of sha256 over the normalized statement. Two memories with the same normalized statement share an id (that is how exact restatements fold).

statement.description: MODEL-EMITTED one-line assertion of the thing to remember — terse and self-contained. May be a reconciled/synthesized rephrasing of several member memories.

description.description: MODEL-EMITTED optional longer prose companion to `statement` (2-4 sentences: the why/symptom/consequence/nuance the terse statement cannot carry). Null when not emitted.

type.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-validated) PRIMARY kind of memory. `decision` carries its adopted-vs-rejected outcome in `decision_outcome`; `intention` is a captured 'we should do X' nudge that is held for review, never loaded without a human check. A memory that is genuinely two kinds at once may also carry a `secondary_type`.

secondary_type.description: MODEL-EMITTED optional SECOND kind of memory — a single field (never a list) for a memory that is genuinely two types at once (e.g. a config choice that is both a `decision` and a `fact`). One of the same type values, and always distinct from the primary `type`; null when the memory is a single kind. The primary `type` remains authoritative — provenance/routing keys on it, not on this.

scope.description: CODE-ASSEMBLED nested scope: `identified` is where the memory was OBSERVED; `applicable` is where it APPLIES when that differs (null in the common case).

identified.description: The IDENTIFIED scope — where the memory was OBSERVED.

level.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-derived/validated) fixed-enum breadth of where the memory was observed. Pairs with `ref` (the specific target).

ref.description: MODEL-EMITTED specific target the identified scope points at, in ONE consistent format per level: personal -> null; dir -> the directory path; service -> the BARE service name, lowercased, no owner/repo qualifier (e.g. 'billing'); repo -> '<owner>/<repo>' (e.g. 'acme/shop'); team -> the team name; org -> the provider or org name (e.g. 'aws', 'acme'), which need not be the user's own org. Null for `personal`.

applicable.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-carried on merge) optional APPLICABLE scope — where the memory APPLIES, when that differs from the identified scope it was observed at (e.g. a dir-level convention that actually holds repo-wide). Null when applicability equals the identified scope (the common case), so a non-null object always means 'applies somewhere other than where it was seen'.

level.description: The applicable-scope breadth. Same fixed enum as the identified level.

ref.description: Target of the applicable scope, using the same per-level `ref` convention as the identified scope. Null for `personal`.

tags.description: CODE-COMBINED typed tag object over six axes; every axis is always present. Two axes are single-valued (domain, activity; null when the memory carries none); four are open, multi-valued lists (component, tech, concept, keyword; keyword is the catch-all). The extraction model proposes each memory's tags; an answer given as a list of strings such as `tech:go` is decoded into this object. On reconcile the single-value axes take the first non-null value in member order; on merge the majority value. Under both rules every other value moves to keyword, so nothing is dropped. Open axes are unioned (distinct, first-seen order). Never authored by the reconcile or synthesis model.

domain.description: Single-valued top-level subject area. OPEN VALUE — there is no hardcoded vocabulary; any short label the model chose (e.g. 'ci-cd', 'backend', 'database'). Null if the memory carries no domain.

activity.description: Single-valued: the work mode in which a future agent should see this memory. At extraction the model picks from a closed list (coding, reviewing, debugging, deploying, planning, incident, onboarding, researching, analyzing, experimenting, training, operating, writing, designing) or null; the merged output does not re-check the list. A second mode belongs in the open `concept` axis, not a second activity.

component.description: Open, multi-valued: named components, modules, services or tools the memory touches (e.g. 'cart-service').

tech.description: Open, multi-valued: technologies, languages, frameworks or vendors (e.g. 'go', 'postgres', 'nextjs').

concept.description: Open, multi-valued: concepts, ideas or patterns the memory is about (e.g. 'idempotency', 'rate-limiting').

keyword.description: Open, multi-valued CATCH-ALL: free keywords that fit no other axis, plus any single-value-axis value demoted during a merge conflict (so a losing domain/activity is preserved here rather than dropped).

generality.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-validated) whether the memory is a one-off instance fact or a reusable principle.

review.description: CODE-STAMPED: whether the memory is safe to load without a human check. An `intention` is always forced to hold-for-review; everything else defaults to active.

status.description: active = safe to load without a human check; hold-for-review = captured, but a human checks it before it is loaded (always so for intentions).

intention_meta.description: MODEL-EMITTED, for `type: intention` only: what to do and how to know it is done. Null for every other type.

what.description: The intended action ('we should do X').

done_check.description: How to tell the intention has been carried out.

decision_outcome.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-carried on merge) a `decision`'s outcome: what was adopted and what was rejected. On merge it is carried from the latest-dated decision member, and divergent outcomes are flagged in the text. Null for non-decisions.

temporal.description: CODE-CARRIED (from members, latest-wins) grouped temporal rich-meta: the decay class, coarse rot-speed, and the free anchor for when the fact was asserted true. All three default null and travel as a coherent unit from the most-recent member.

kind.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-softened) decay class of the memory. Unknown values coerce to null rather than dropping the memory.

volatility.description: MODEL-EMITTED (code-softened) coarse rot-speed heuristic — how fast this memory is likely to go stale. Null when not emitted.

valid_as_of.description: MODEL-EMITTED free anchor for when the fact was asserted true (e.g. '2026-05-12'), resolved against the session date. Not an enum. Null when the window gives no anchor.

disposition.description: CODE-CARRIED human-review trust — a DIFFERENT axis from provenance.confidence. On merge a memory is borderline if any covered member is borderline UNLESS >=2 distinct conversations corroborate it (independent conversations resolve a single-source doubt).

note.description: Reason a memory is borderline (carried from the first borderline member); empty string when confident. Always a string, never null.

provenance.description: CODE-STAMPED grouped provenance: the memory-level confidence annotation plus the independent-support corroboration counts.

confidence.description: CODE-STAMPED annotation (not a filter): how well the memory's evidence quotes are authored for its type, over their per-quote effective authorship. `high` = every quote is admissibly and positively authored (human_prose for preference, convention and intention; human_prose, model_generated or tool_output for fact, decision, caution and failed-attempt); `uncertain` = no positively inadmissible quote, but at least one lacks a signal (unknown or null); `low` = at least one quote is positively inadmissible (template_boilerplate for any type; tool_output or model_generated for preference, convention or intention). Recomputed on merge from the final evidence set against the final type. Nothing is dropped for it.

corroboration.description: CODE-STAMPED (merge only) independent-support counts. Only distinct CONVERSATIONS corroborate — two arms reading the same conversation is one source seen twice, not two.

distinct_arms.description: How many distinct extraction arms produced a member of this memory.

distinct_conversations.description: How many distinct source conversations back this memory.

source_arms.description: The distinct arms (`facts`, `preferences`), in that order.

source_conversation_ids.description: The distinct source conversation ids, sorted.

evidence.description: MODEL-PROPOSED, CODE-VERIFIED supporting quotes. Every item passed the evidence gate: the quote matches the cited turn once case, whitespace, curly quotes and NFKC compatibility forms are folded, spoken by the cited speaker, in that source conversation. A memory with no surviving evidence is dropped, so this is never empty.

quote.description: The stretch of the cited turn the quote matched, as the session holds it.

turn.description: 1-based index of the turn the quote came from.

speaker.description: Role that spoke the cited turn; an assistant quote can never back a person-attributed memory.

conversation_id.description: Which source conversation the quote came from, so every quote stays traceable.

arm.description: CODE-STAMPED which extraction arm (`facts` or `preferences`) contributed this evidence item.

authorship.description: CODE-STAMPED per-quote effective authorship (the carried inner authorship when the quote falls solely within an envelope's inner span, else the turn's own): human_prose | model_generated | template_boilerplate | tool_output | unknown. Null when the turn could not be attributed. Feeds `provenance.confidence`.
